content: The defining characteristic of hepatic encephalopathy is the accumulation of ammonia and other toxic substances in the bloodstream, which are typically detoxified by the liver under normal conditions. A history of cirrhosis or acute viral hepatitis is indicative of hepatic encephalopathy. The most frequently observed symptoms of hepatic encephalopathy include cognitive dysfunction, alterations in personality, and, in severe cases, progression to coma. Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a prevalent complication in patients with liver cirrhosis. It is associated with distinct alterations in cerebral metabolite patterns, which can be detected using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS). A history of alcohol consumption and viral hepatitis is also suggestive of hepatic encephalopathy.
